correctness.rationale: Canonical order-simplex triangulation is indexed by Dyck words (two chains, dominance A_i≺B_i); each simplex has volume 1/(2n)!. Coordinate facets have intrinsic area 1/(D−1)! and cover-equality facets √2/(D−1)! because the latter equality normal has length √2; face adjacency occurs exactly when the cover elements are consecutive in the linear extension. In a Dyck word peaks UD, valleys DU, hills UD at level zero, only hills correspond to the vertical cover A_i≺B_i. Its number of cover adjacencies is D−2P+H. Narayana symmetry E[P]=(n+1)/2 and Catalan-convolution E[H]=1, so all cover faces total D√2 n, split horizontal D√2(n−1), vertical D√2. A hill at i corresponds to C_{i−1}C_{n−i} words, giving each vertical area. Terminal coordinate facets add 2D. Catalan asymptotics C_n~4^n/(√π n^(3/2)) prove endpoint q_i=C_{i−1}/4^i, total half each, the specified bulk density and tails. Direct new rational Catalan probability checks for n=2,3,4,5,8 sum to one and respect symmetry; they are not all-n certificates.
